channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Can traditional Chinese exercises help people with musculoskeletal disorders? - BJSM blog - social media's leading SEM voice
item.description: An umbrella review of 92 meta-analyses of RCTs found high-certainty evidence that traditional Chinese exercises improved physical function and mental health in knee osteoarthritis, mental health in neck pain, and sleep quality in fibromyalgia, with Tai Chi showing the most consistent benefits.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Effects of Exercise Type and Duration on Pain, Function, and Quality of Life in Patients With Knee Osteoarthritis: A Systematic Review With Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A network meta-analysis of 35 trials (N=3808) found that short-term combined aerobic and resistance exercise had the largest effects on pain (SMD = -0.937, low certainty), function (SMD = -0.590, low certainty), and quality of life (SMD = 0.663, low certainty) in knee osteoarthritis patients.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Interval Between Injury and Surgery Influences Knee Biomechanics During Walking in Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstructed Patients: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 studies found that delayed ACL reconstruction (≥12 months) is associated with persistent sagittal plane deficits in walking biomechanics, while early surgery (<6 months) correlates with fewer long-term sagittal-plane deficits but may have temporary frontal-plane asymmetries.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative Effects of Neurostimulation- and Technology-Augmented Robot-Assisted Training on Upper-Limb Motor Recovery After Stroke: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A network meta-analysis of 103 trials (5,251 participants) found rTMS plus robot-assisted training yielded the largest Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity estimate (MD = 9.56) for poststroke upper-limb recovery, followed by low-frequency electrical stimulation plus RAT (MD = 7.52), compared to usual care.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Altered Cognitive Control and Cortical Oscillatory Dynamics in Athletes With ACL Reconstruction During Decision-Making Under Uncertainty.
item.description: A controlled laboratory study of 90 open-skill athletes (45 non-ACLR, 45 ACLR) found ACLR athletes showed slower response times, lower accuracy, and altered cortical oscillatory dynamics (attenuated prestimulus theta, elevated target phase theta, reduced beta/alpha suppression) during a probabilistic go/no-go task.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Efficacy of Manual Physiotherapy Techniques for Improving Cervical Range of Motion in Infants With Congenital Muscular Torticollis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of five RCTs (n=143 infants) found manual physiotherapy techniques significantly improved cervical ROM in infants with congenital muscular torticollis (Cohen's d = 0.90, 95% CI: 0.54 to 1.27, p < 0.001), indicating a large overall effect with low heterogeneity.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Diagnosis, Rehabilitation, and Return to Sport after Athletic Hamstring Injury: An ICCUS Society Consensus Statement.
item.description: An ICCUS Society expert consensus statement, developed via a modified Delphi process with 17 clinicians, achieved over 80% agreement on 54 statements concerning athletic hamstring injury management, emphasizing standardized classification, individualized criterion-based rehabilitation, progressive loading, and multi-faceted return-to-sport criteria.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Gait variability as a predictor of fall risk in patients with stroke: A 6-month prospective cohort study with survival analysis.
item.description: In a 6-month prospective cohort study of 112 stroke patients, stride time variability (STV) at discharge, with an optimal cutoff of 3.40% (AUC 0.756, sensitivity 88.2%, specificity 53.8%), was identified as the sole independent predictor of post-discharge falls, outperforming conventional measures.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of chair-based exercise training on pulmonary function, exercise capacity, and quality of life in patients with acute exacerbation of COPD: A randomised controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial of 30 AECOPD patients found that chair-based exercise training significantly improved functional exercise capacity (79.7m vs 28.8m in 6MWT), dyspnoea, and quality of life compared to breathing exercises alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Five Days of Acute Intermittent Hypoxia Is Safe and Improves Somatic Motor Function in Persons with Multiple Sclerosis
item.description: A randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled crossover trial in ambulatory MS patients found daily acute intermittent hypoxia (AIH) was safe and significantly improved ankle plantarflexion torque (17.5% post-intervention, 29.2% at follow-up) and 6-Minute Walk Test distance (β=10.14 m, p=0.039) compared to sham.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Neurocognitive Factors in ACL Injury: The Missing Piece in Rehabilitation and Prevention? A Scoping Review.
item.description: A scoping review of 42 studies identified neurocognitive factors, particularly dual-task interference and visual attention, as significant missing components in ACL injury rehabilitation and prevention. It suggests integrating neurocognitive challenges into rehabilitation and return-to-sport testing to better identify secondary injury risk.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative Efficacy of Low-Level Laser Therapy in Patients With Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.description: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 RCTs found low-level laser therapy (LLLT) significantly reduced pain (Hedges' g=-1.524, P <0.001) and improved grip strength (Hedges' g=0.391, P=0.002) in carpal tunnel syndrome. Pulsed mode was superior for analgesia, continuous for grip strength.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: First-Hand Experience and the Value of Telerehabilitation for Chronic Knee Pain: A Discrete Choice Experiment Nested in a Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: Australian adults (N=319) with chronic knee pain who experienced telerehabilitation were willing to pay AU$87.49 (95% CI: 72.83, 102.14) more for telerehabilitation consultations than those who received in-person care.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Inertial measurement unit-based gait analysis for objective assessment of vestibular rehabilitation.
item.description: IMU-based gait analysis, even with a single pelvis sensor, captured significant improvements in walking speed, Gait Profile Score, and cadence in 30 acute vestibular syndrome patients after 6 weeks of vestibular rehabilitation, maintained at 12 weeks.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physiotherapy and Exercise-Based Rehabilitation for Mental Health: A Two-Decade Bibliometric Analysis of Global Trends, Thematic Evolution, and the Socioeconomic Vulnerability Gap (2006-2025).
item.description: A bibliometric analysis of 5223 publications (2006-2025) on physical rehabilitation and mental health found a 22.6-fold increase in annual publications, with 75.9% originating from high-income countries and socioeconomic vulnerability identified as an under-researched thematic cluster.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Early Prediction of Discharge Outcomes in Geriatric Rehabilitation: Development and Temporal Validation of a Multiclass Model
item.description: A multiclass prediction model developed using multinomial regression and XGBoost accurately predicted discharge outcomes (minimal dependency, nursing-care dependency, or medical deterioration) in 10,920 geriatric rehabilitation patients by day 7, achieving an AUC of 0.81.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Effects of low-dose cervical paraspinal lidocaine injections on cervicogenic dizziness-related outcomes: a randomized, sham-controlled, assessor-blinded trial.
item.description: A randomized, sham-controlled trial (n=81) found low-dose cervical paraspinal lidocaine injections improved Dizziness Handicap Inventory total scores by -6.78 points (95% CI -8.21 to -5.36; p < 0.001) more than sham, but this was below the 11-point minimal important change for cervicogenic dizziness.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Ultrasound-guided versus landmark-guided injections in musculoskeletal practice: a scoping review of clinical efficacy, educational needs, and economic considerations
item.description: A scoping review of 29 studies found ultrasound-guided (US) injections reliably improve placement accuracy and may provide short-term symptomatic benefit at selected sites (shoulder, knee, elbow). However, comparative clinical superiority at longer follow-up and cost-effectiveness remain undetermined.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Feasibility, Safety, and Preliminary Effect Estimates of an Ultrasound-Informed Hybrid Joint-Sparing Rehabilitation Strategy in Patients With Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Prospective Non-Randomized Proof-of-Concept Study.
item.description: A 12-week ultrasound-informed hybrid rehabilitation protocol for rheumatoid arthritis was found feasible and safe in 60 patients, showing greater pain reduction (ΔVAS: -2.88 cm vs. -0.60 cm; p < 0.001) than a control group, though effect sizes may be overestimated and specific ultrasound attribution was limited.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Walking Capacity and Daily Movement Behaviours After Ischemic Stroke: A Potential Capacity-Performance Gap.
item.description: A cross-sectional study of ambulatory ischemic stroke patients found a capacity-performance gap: participants accumulated ~12 hours/day of sedentary time despite walking speeds approaching community ambulation, with gait speed being the only walking capacity measure associated with daily movement behaviors.
item.author: PubMed
